_comment: Reference sequences and bioactive motifs for sequence-based identification. This is a curated local cache, not an authority: every entry should be confirmed against UniProt or primary literature before being relied on. Sequences are included only where well established; uncertain ones were left out rather than approximated, because a wrong sequence produces confidently wrong downstream analysis. Peptides containing non-canonical residues (D-amino acids, Aib, beta-alanine, pyroglutamate, amidation) cannot be fully represented in one-letter code and are noted where included.

GLP-1 (7-37).function: Incretin hormone: glucose-dependent insulin secretion, satiety, delayed gastric emptying via GLP-1R
GLP-1 (7-37).goal_reason: Native GLP-1 has a ~2 minute half-life due to DPP-4 cleavage at position 2. Protease resistance is the dominant liability.

GLP-1 (7-36) amide.function: The predominant circulating GLP-1 form; amidated C-terminus
GLP-1 (7-36) amide.goal_reason: Same DPP-4 liability at position 2 as GLP-1(7-37); already C-terminally amidated.

GLP-2.function: Intestinotrophic hormone: promotes intestinal mucosal growth via GLP-2R
GLP-2.goal_reason: DPP-4 substrate; teduglutide is the clinical analog stabilised at position 2.

Glucagon.function: Counter-regulatory hormone: raises blood glucose via GCGR
Glucagon.goal_reason: Shares the DPP-4-susceptible N-terminus of the glucagon superfamily; also poorly soluble at neutral pH.

Oxyntomodulin.function: Dual GLP-1R/GCGR agonist: reduces food intake and increases energy expenditure
Oxyntomodulin.goal_reason: DPP-4 substrate with a very short half-life; the basis of dual-agonist programmes.

GIP (1-42).function: Glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide: incretin acting via GIPR
GIP (1-42).goal_reason: Cleaved by DPP-4 at position 2; tirzepatide uses Aib at that position.

Exendin-4 (exenatide).function: GLP-1R agonist from Gila monster venom; naturally DPP-4 resistant via Gly at position 2
Exendin-4 (exenatide).goal_reason: Already DPP-4 resistant (Gly2), so proteolysis is not the limiting property; the Trp-cage C-terminal extension drives receptor affinity.

Insulin A-chain.function: A-chain of insulin; disulfide-linked to the B-chain in the mature hormone
Insulin A-chain.goal_reason: An isolated chain is not the functional unit — the cysteines form interchain disulfides.

Insulin B-chain.function: B-chain of insulin; carries the receptor-binding surface and the hexamer interface
Insulin B-chain.goal_reason: B28-B29 determine monomer/hexamer equilibrium — the basis of fast-acting analogs (lispro, aspart).

Amylin (IAPP).function: Co-secreted with insulin; slows gastric emptying and suppresses glucagon
Amylin (IAPP).goal_reason: Human amylin is strongly amyloidogenic — the 20-29 region drives fibril formation. Pramlintide substitutes prolines there.

PYY (3-36).function: Anorexigenic gut hormone acting on the Y2 receptor
PYY (3-36).goal_reason: Itself a DPP-4 product of PYY(1-36); further degraded in circulation.

Neuropeptide Y.function: Orexigenic neuropeptide; also vasoconstrictive via Y1
Neuropeptide Y.goal_reason: DPP-4 converts NPY(1-36) to NPY(3-36), switching receptor selectivity from Y1 to Y2 — proteolysis changes function, not just duration.

Ghrelin (human).function: Orexigenic hormone; requires Ser3 octanoylation for GHSR activity
Ghrelin (human).goal_reason: The Ser3 octanoyl ester is rapidly hydrolysed by esterases, which inactivates the peptide independently of proteolysis.

Oxytocin.function: Uterine contraction, milk ejection, social bonding via OXTR
Oxytocin.goal_reason: Short disulfide-cyclised nonapeptide with a very short plasma half-life.

Vasopressin (AVP).function: Antidiuresis and vasoconstriction via V1/V2 receptors
Vasopressin (AVP).goal_reason: Short half-life; desmopressin (dDAVP) is the clinical precedent for stabilising this scaffold.

Substance P.function: NK1 receptor agonist: pain transmission, neurogenic inflammation
Substance P.goal_reason: Degraded by neprilysin and ACE; the C-terminal Met is also an oxidation liability.

Bradykinin.function: Vasodilation, vascular permeability, pain via the B2 receptor
Bradykinin.goal_reason: Half-life under a minute; degraded by ACE and neprilysin.

Angiotensin II.function: Vasoconstriction and aldosterone release via AT1
Angiotensin II.goal_reason: Rapidly cleaved by aminopeptidases and ACE2.

Angiotensin I.function: Inactive precursor converted to angiotensin II by ACE
Angiotensin I.goal_reason: Its function is to be cleaved — ACE removes the C-terminal His-Leu.

Met-enkephalin.goal_reason: Half-life of minutes; degraded by enkephalinase (neprilysin) and aminopeptidase N. The C-terminal Met also oxidises.

Leu-enkephalin.goal_reason: Same rapid enkephalinase and aminopeptidase degradation as Met-enkephalin.

Dynorphin A (1-17).goal_reason: Highly cationic and rapidly processed; the YGGFL N-terminus is the opioid pharmacophore.

Beta-endorphin.function: Endogenous mu opioid agonist derived from POMC
Beta-endorphin.goal_reason: Long for an opioid peptide; the YGGFM N-terminus carries the pharmacophore and is the exopeptidase entry point.

Somatostatin-14.function: Inhibits growth hormone, insulin and glucagon release via SSTR1-5
Somatostatin-14.goal_reason: Half-life of ~3 minutes; octreotide is the stabilised D-amino-acid analog.

GnRH (LHRH).function: Stimulates LH and FSH release from the pituitary
GnRH (LHRH).goal_reason: Cleaved at Gly6-Leu7; all clinical analogs substitute position 6, typically with a D-amino acid.

alpha-MSH.function: Melanocortin receptor agonist: pigmentation, appetite, inflammation
alpha-MSH.goal_reason: The HFRW core is the pharmacophore; Met4 is an oxidation liability.

ACTH (1-24).function: Adrenocorticotropic fragment retaining full steroidogenic activity
ACTH (1-24).goal_reason: Shares the alpha-MSH HFRW core plus the polybasic 15-24 extension that drives MC2R affinity.

Calcitonin (salmon).function: Inhibits osteoclast-mediated bone resorption; more potent than the human form
Calcitonin (salmon).goal_reason: Salmon calcitonin fibrillates readily in solution, which is the main formulation problem.

CGRP (alpha, human).function: Potent vasodilator; central to migraine pathophysiology
CGRP (alpha, human).goal_reason: Receptor identity depends on RAMP1 association with CLR — the accessory subunit determines the pharmacology.

TRH.goal_reason: A tripeptide whose N-terminal pyroglutamate and C-terminal amide are both required; cleaved by TRH-degrading ectoenzyme.

Bombesin.function: GRP receptor agonist: stimulates gastrin release, mitogenic in several tumours
Bombesin.goal_reason: The C-terminal WAVGHLM heptapeptide is the pharmacophore; Met is an oxidation liability.

DSIP.function: Delta sleep-inducing peptide; reported sleep-modulating and stress-protective activity
DSIP.goal_reason: Small, highly anionic, and rapidly cleared; mechanistic evidence remains limited.

LL-37.function: Human cathelicidin: membrane-disrupting antimicrobial and immunomodulator
LL-37.goal_reason: Cationic amphipathic helix. Activity depends on the amphipathic fold, and it is salt-sensitive and protease-labile.

Magainin 2.function: Amphibian antimicrobial peptide; forms toroidal pores in bacterial membranes
Magainin 2.goal_reason: Classic cationic amphipathic helix — activity is fold-dependent, so constraint moves apply alongside stability.

Melittin.function: Principal cytolytic component of bee venom; lyses both bacterial and mammalian membranes
Melittin.goal_reason: Potently haemolytic as well as antimicrobial — the problem is selectivity for bacterial over mammalian membranes, not potency.

Indolicidin.goal_reason: Five tryptophans make this exceptionally oxidation- and photo-sensitive.

HNP-1 (alpha-defensin 1).function: Neutrophil alpha-defensin: antimicrobial, three disulfide bonds
HNP-1 (alpha-defensin 1).goal_reason: Six cysteines in a defined connectivity make it already protease-stable; correct disulfide pairing is the real constraint.

BPC-157.function: Synthetic pentadecapeptide from a gastric juice protein fragment; reported in tissue-repair models
BPC-157.goal_reason: Reported stability in gastric juice is its distinguishing claim, so proteolytic behaviour is what is worth examining. Human clinical evidence is limited.

Thymosin beta-4.function: Actin-sequestering peptide; reported to accelerate wound closure and angiogenesis
Thymosin beta-4.goal_reason: Highly charged and intrinsically disordered, so it is broadly protease-accessible.

GHK.function: Copper-binding tripeptide; reported to stimulate collagen synthesis and wound repair
GHK.goal_reason: Activity depends on Cu(II) chelation by the His imidazole and the N-terminal amine — the metal complex is the active species.

Matrixyl (KTTKS).function: Procollagen I C-terminal fragment; feedback signal stimulating collagen synthesis
Matrixyl (KTTKS).goal_reason: A pentapeptide with free termini is a straightforward exopeptidase substrate; the palmitoylated form is used for skin penetration.

Argireline (acetyl hexapeptide-3).function: SNAP-25 N-terminal mimetic; competitively interferes with SNARE complex assembly
Argireline (acetyl hexapeptide-3).goal_reason: Acts by competing with SNAP-25 for the SNARE complex, so affinity for that interface is the limiting property.

Semax.function: ACTH(4-7) analog with a Pro-Gly-Pro extension; reported nootropic and neuroprotective
Semax.goal_reason: The C-terminal Pro-Gly-Pro was added specifically to slow degradation of the ACTH(4-7) core.

Selank.function: Tuftsin (TKPR) analog with a Pro-Gly-Pro extension; reported anxiolytic
Selank.goal_reason: Same Pro-Gly-Pro stabilisation strategy as Semax applied to the tuftsin core.

Tuftsin.function: Phagocytosis-stimulating tetrapeptide from the IgG Fc region
Tuftsin.goal_reason: A free tetrapeptide is rapidly cleaved by aminopeptidases.

Epitalon.function: Synthetic tetrapeptide; reported telomerase-modulating and geroprotective activity
Epitalon.goal_reason: A free tetrapeptide with minimal structure; mechanistic evidence is limited.

Glutathione.goal_reason: The gamma-linkage between Glu and Cys is what makes it resistant to ordinary aminopeptidases — a standard alpha-peptide of this sequence is not glutathione.

Carnosine.function: Beta-alanyl-histidine: antioxidant and pH buffer in muscle and brain
Carnosine.goal_reason: Cleaved by serum carnosinase. Note the beta-alanine is not representable in one-letter code, so this entry is an approximation of the residue identity only.

TAT (47-57).function: HIV-1 TAT protein transduction domain; carries cargo across membranes
TAT (47-57).goal_reason: Extremely cationic and trypsin-labile — eight of eleven residues are Arg or Lys.

Penetratin.function: Antennapedia homeodomain third helix; cell-penetrating peptide
Penetratin.goal_reason: Cationic and trypsin-labile; uptake depends on the amphipathic helical character.

Polyarginine (R8).goal_reason: Every residue is a trypsin P1 site. D-arginine versions are the standard fix.

IKVAV.function: Neurite outgrowth, cell adhesion and migration; widely used to functionalise neural scaffolds
IKVAV.goal_reason: A short adhesion motif from a very large basement-membrane protein. Activity is presentation-dependent — density, spacing and multivalency dominate over half-life.
IKVAV.native_context_note: Internal fragment of a multi-thousand-residue ECM protein. Both termini are excision artefacts, and natively the motif sits on a folded domain.

YIGSR.function: Cell adhesion via the 67 kDa laminin receptor; reported anti-metastatic and anti-angiogenic
YIGSR.goal_reason: Adhesion motif whose activity depends on receptor engagement and presentation rather than circulating exposure.
YIGSR.native_context_note: Internal fragment of laminin beta-1; free termini are excision artefacts.

RKRLQVQLSIRT.function: Syndecan binding; cell adhesion, spreading and neurite outgrowth
RKRLQVQLSIRT.goal_reason: Syndecan binding is charge-driven, so charge engineering and presentation dominate over proteolytic stability.
RKRLQVQLSIRT.native_context_note: Internal fragment of the laminin alpha-1 LG4 module; strongly cationic, which is the basis of its syndecan binding.

PHSRN.function: Synergy site that cooperates with RGD for alpha5beta1 integrin binding
PHSRN.goal_reason: Only functional at a defined spacing from an RGD motif — the geometry between the two sites is the design variable.
PHSRN.native_context_note: Internal fragment of fibronectin; acts together with RGD rather than alone.

RGD.goal_reason: Integrin subtype selectivity depends almost entirely on the conformation the RGD is presented in — cyclic and linear RGD differ by orders of magnitude.
RGD.native_context_note: A three-residue motif is not specific on its own; flanking residues and conformational constraint determine which integrin it engages.
RGD.min_length_warning: 'RGD' is only 3 residues. A match indicates the motif is present, not that the peptide's function is adhesion.

REDV.goal_reason: Selected for endothelial selectivity over platelet adhesion, so selectivity rather than raw affinity is the objective.
REDV.native_context_note: Internal fragment of the fibronectin IIICS region.
REDV.min_length_warning: 'REDV' is only 4 residues. A match indicates the motif is present, not that the peptide's function is adhesion.

DGEA.goal_reason: Collagen-mimetic adhesion depends on triple-helical presentation, which a linear peptide does not reproduce.
DGEA.native_context_note: Excised from a triple-helical protein; the isolated linear peptide lacks the native conformation.
DGEA.min_length_warning: 'DGEA' is only 4 residues. A match indicates the motif is present, not that the peptide's function is adhesion.

family_signatures._comment: Physicochemical signatures used when no sequence or motif match is found. These are heuristics over computed Tier 0 properties and are reported as INFERRED, never as identification.

cationic_amphipathic_amp.description: Cationic amphipathic helix — the host-defence / antimicrobial peptide profile
cationic_amphipathic_amp.goal_reason: Antimicrobial peptides are typically protease-labile and lose activity on proteolysis. Activity also depends on the amphipathic fold, so constraint moves are the other productive direction.

disulfide_rich.description: Disulfide-rich scaffold — defensin, knottin, or growth-factor-like fold
disulfide_rich.goal_reason: Disulfide-rich scaffolds are already proteolytically stable because of their crosslinked fold, so protease resistance is rarely the limiting property. Binding and correct disulfide pairing dominate.

collagen_like.goal_reason: Gly/Pro-rich sequences are MMP and collagenase substrates.
